cur:catacombs-ravenna-isaac-sarcophagus.summary: On the front, three Magi in fluttering cloaks hurry with their gifts towards the Virgin, who holds the Christ Child on her lap at the left. The sarcophagus, carved in the 5th century, was reused in the 7th for the Armenian exarch Isaac, and its lively relief contrasts with the sober barrel-vaulted lid.
facts: Isaac the Armenian was exarch of Ravenna (c. 625–643); his tomb is in San Vitale.
Wikipedia notes that the sarcophagus also shows Daniel and Lazarus.
cur:catacombs-ravenna-isaac-sarcophagus.notes: The 5th-century date of the carving is the usual view; the reuse dates to Isaac's death.

cur:monumental-mustair-pilate.summary: Within a painted frame of coloured bands, Pilate sits enthroned at the left as a servant pours water over his hands, while Christ stands at the right, haloed and silent, before his judge. The pale, partly faded painting belongs to the Passion register on the south wall.
facts: The abbey of Saint John at Müstair, founded c. 780, preserves wall paintings of about 800 arranged in five registers: the life of David at the top, three rows on the youth, ministry and Passion of Christ, and below them scenes of Saint Andrew, joined on the west wall by a Last Judgment.
UNESCO, which inscribed the abbey in 1983, describes them as Switzerland's greatest series of figurative murals, painted around 800.

cur:monumental-red-monastery-theotokos.summary: In the semi-dome of the north apse, the enthroned Virgin nurses the Christ Child on her lap, flanked by archangels, while prophets in the zone around and below hold open scrolls with Sahidic Coptic texts of prophecies concerning her. The warm golden light of the restored painting fills the triconch sanctuary, whose every surface is painted.
facts: The Red Monastery's triconch sanctuary is described as the only monumental ensemble of architecture, sculpture and fully painted surfaces surviving from late antiquity in the Mediterranean; its paint dates between the late 5th and the late 6th or early 7th century.
The church was built as a basilica in the second half of the 5th century, architecturally similar to the nearby White Monastery church of Shenoute.
cur:monumental-red-monastery-theotokos.notes: The exact date of this image within the successive painting campaigns is not confirmed here.
